sentences.text: for the offences punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376(2)(n) of IPC and Sections 4, 6, 8, 12, 16 & 17 of the POCSO Act, 2012, is before this Court with a prayer to quash the entire proceedings in the said case as against him.
2. Learned Counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner has married the victim girl.
The victim girl is a major and her date of birth is 18.03.2003 and in support of this contention of his, he has placed reliance on the photostat copy of the birth certificate of the victim girl.
Since the victim is a major, the petitioner cannot be prosecuted for the alleged offences.
Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition.
Per contra, learned HCGP and the learned Counsel for respondent no.2 have opposed the petition.

Learned Counsel for respondent no.2 has produced the SSLC marks card of the victim girl along with school transfer certificate and submits that the date of birth of the victim girl is 18.03.2006 and on the date of marriage, the victim was a minor, and therefore, the alleged offences get attracted against the petitioner.
Accordingly, he prays to dismiss the petition.

sentences.text: The first informant who is the father of the victim girl aged about 17 years had initially submitted the first information on 17.01.2024 alleging that his minor daughter aged about 17 years was found missing from the house.
Since she was found talking to the petitioner over phone, he had suspected the hand of the petitioner, and therefore, the first information was initially registered against the petitioner.

5. During the course of investigation, petitioner and the victim girl were traced and the statement of the victim girl under Section 164 Cr.PC was recorded by the jurisdictional Magistrate on 14.02.2024,
wherein the victim girl has stated that she is aged about 17 years, and on 16.01.2024, petitioner NC:

2025:KHC-K:933 who came near her house took her along with him and they got married in the Madarasa.
6.

According to the learned Counsel for the petitioner, the victim girl was a major and in support of this contention of his, he has placed reliance on the photostat copy of the birth certificate of the victim girl.

On the other hand, learned Counsel for respondent no.2 has produced the marks card of the victim girl issued by Karnataka Secondary Education Examination Board and in the said marks card, the date of birth of the victim girl is mentioned as 18.03.2006.
Therefore, it is for the petitioner to prove during the course of trial that the victim girl was major as on the date of alleged incident.
Since there are documents which show the date of birth of the victim girl as 18.03.2006, at this stage, it cannot be said that the petitioner cannot be prosecuted for the charge-sheeted offences.
Under the circumstances, I do not find any good ground to entertain this petition.

Accordingly,
petition is dismissed.
